turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Good morning, this is The Morning Commute. Monday, November 23. I'm Sam.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: And I'm Alex. We start in Antalya, where the world's climate talks ran 2 days past their deadline and then simply stopped, with no deal at all.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: COP31 closed in the early hours of Sunday without a cover decision, the political text that every COP since Copenhagen in 2009 has managed to produce. It's being called the longest COP on record. The break came when the EU and the Pacific island states rejected a final draft that had been stripped of any language on fossil fuels, after pressure from oil producers. Climate finance was the other wall. The Turkish presidency's Murat Kurum said simply that there was no agreement on the text, António Guterres said he was deeply disappointed, and Australia's Chris Bowen, who co-led the talks, blamed unbridgeable red lines.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The fine print matters here. Nothing agreed in Dubai or Belém is undone, so the transition-away-from-fossil-fuels language from 2023 still stands on paper. What died is the forward step. And the bloc that walked away was the one that usually bends to get a deal. The EU decided that a text with no fossil language was worse than no text, which tells you the process now has a veto on both ends: producers can block ambition, and the ambitious can block retreat.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: To the Gulf, where attacks on shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz are now at their highest level since the Iran war began, according to CNN's tally. The maritime risk firm Marisks says projectiles hit 3 tankers leaving the strait on Friday and Saturday, and one of them, the Captain Leon, caught fire at the bow. Iranian media tell it differently: 2 tankers hit mines north of Ghanam Island after switching off their transponders and entering what Tehran calls a restricted zone. Britain's UKMTO logged a separate incident in the Gulf of Oman involving what it called military forces, and the Houthis are now threatening Saudi Red Sea ports.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Mines or missiles is not a detail. Missiles are a decision you can deter; mines are a standing condition you have to clear, and clearing takes weeks of minehunters working under fire. That's the scenario insurers price hardest. The odd part is that Brent still logged its third straight weekly fall, to 92.57 dollars, because the equity panic swamped everything. If the tanker count keeps climbing into December, that's a risk premium that hasn't been charged yet.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: And Spain enters its last week before Sunday's snap election under a polling blackout. The final 40dB tracker for El País had the People's Party ahead of Pedro Sánchez's Socialists by less than a point, after an earlier read of 31.9% to 31.2%. Sigma Dos has it wider: the PP on 30.8% and 126 seats, the PSOE on 26.1% and 110. Alberto Núñez Feijóo won last Wednesday's debate 43 to 33 in 40dB's snap poll, and prediction markets give him an 87.5% chance of becoming prime minister.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The arithmetic is the story: 176 seats for a majority, and only the PP plus Vox gets there, at 192 in the Sigma Dos model. So the realistic outcome is a Feijóo government that leans on the hard right, in a country that has been the euro zone's growth leader. Sánchez's last card is rent control, which polls well, and the fear of Vox in government, which mobilises his base.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: In US business, private equity is shopping the wreckage. TPG and Corpay are taking BILL Holdings private for 63.25 dollars a share in cash, about 6 billion dollars in total, and that price is below where BILL traded before the deal was announced. Corpay puts in 1.1 billion dollars for roughly a third of the company and gets an option to buy the rest in 2030.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: A take-under tells you the board judged the public market wasn't going to pay more for a small-business payments platform any time soon, and that the private bid was the best number on offer. The Corpay structure is the clever bit: a strategic buyer with a staged path to control, and TPG supplying the balance sheet in between.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: And the week's real test lands Tuesday after the close, when Dell reports. The street is looking for earnings of roughly 6.55 to 6.63 dollars a share on about 50.6 billion dollars of revenue, and it's the first big AI-hardware print since the rout. Best Buy, HP, Workday and Autodesk report the same day, and Wednesday brings October core PCE, expected at 3.2% year on year from 3.1%, plus the second look at third-quarter GDP and Deere. Then Thanksgiving, a half-day Friday, and a National Retail Federation forecast for holiday sales up 4.2% to 1.013 trillion dollars, the first time above a trillion.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Internationally, the European Union's next 7-year budget is in trouble before the leaders even meet. On Saturday, Friedrich Merz said European Council President António Costa's new draft for 2028 to 2034, about 1.78 trillion euros in current prices, is not a basis for an agreement, and Emmanuel Macron reportedly rejected it too. The draft is 44 billion euros smaller than the Irish presidency's October text, and Costa wants new EU-wide revenue, including a digital tax. Berlin opposes both new taxes and new joint borrowing. Leaders meet in Brussels on Thursday and Friday, and it takes unanimity.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The notable thing is that Germany and France are rejecting it from opposite directions. Paris wants more money for farmers and defence; Berlin wants no new taxes and no new debt. My guess is this summit produces a negotiating box, not a number, and the real deal slips into the spring.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: And in Turkey, Istanbul prosecutors have asked for the market holdings of 108 people to be frozen, each of whom allegedly made more than 100 million lira during manipulation windows. It widens a probe into 3 investment funds, in which 214 people and companies are alleged to have taken 187.65 billion lira.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Markets, and this is a numbers day. On Friday the S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910, its seventh straight loss, which put it in correction, more than 10% below the October 6 record. The Nasdaq dropped 5.3% and is now negative for 2026. The S&P lost 8.6% on the week, its worst since April 2025, and the VIX closed near 36.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The trigger was Nvidia, down 14% on Friday, on reports that the SEC is looking at its accounting. The SEC hasn't commented and nothing is confirmed, but after Jensen Huang's exit the market has no patience left for ambiguity. Anthropic, a day after the biggest IPO ever, fell 8.5% to around 89 dollars, close to its 83-dollar offer price. AMD took a short-seller report. And the semiconductor index fell 8.3% in a session.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: The bond market did something different.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The 10-year Treasury yield fell 11 basis points to about 4.93%, the biggest drop since October 22, and swaps stopped pricing a December Fed hike. That's the haven bid finally showing up after a week where yields went up as stocks went down. Gold, meanwhile, fell another 4.6% to about 3,515 dollars, a 14-and-a-half-month low, and Bitcoin broke below 60,000 dollars and touched 55,130 on the weekend. When gold and crypto both fall with stocks, it's deleveraging: people sell what they can, not what they want.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: And this morning?

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: A bounce, at least for now. Tokyo is closed for a holiday. Korea's Kospi was down nearly 6% at one point and tripped a sidecar on program selling, and Taiwan's market rose 2.2% after regulators tightened short-selling rules. Beijing eased margin-financing rules over the weekend, and Seoul says it's ready with stabilisation funds. US futures were up around 2% early, with Nasdaq contracts up nearly 3% and Nvidia up 5.7% premarket. My read: governments in Asia are now treating this as a financial-stability event, not a valuation debate, and that alone tells you how much leverage was in the AI trade. The test is Dell on Tuesday and core PCE on Wednesday. A hot PCE would put the Fed back on the table at exactly the wrong moment.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: For the deep dive, we're leaving markets entirely. The Economist's Sunday newsletter ran a piece headlined: AI may have solved the most important problem in mathematics. Humans spent 167 years trying to prove the Riemann hypothesis. A disclosure first: the claim comes from a mathematician at Anthropic, working with Anthropic's model Claude, and this show is produced with Claude's help too. So weigh our enthusiasm accordingly.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Noted, and it's a good reason to be careful. Here's what happened. On Friday, November 20, Levent Alpöge, a number theorist now employed at Anthropic, posted a 4-page note that begins: I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. He says the same method proves the generalised version for Dirichlet L-functions. And the striking part: there is no human-readable paper. What he released is a proof written in Lean, the formal proof language, spread across 14 archives and reportedly about 17 million lines.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Remind us, briefly, what is actually being claimed.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The Riemann zeta function has infinitely many nontrivial zeros, and the hypothesis says every one of them has real part exactly one half: they all sit on a single vertical line. Riemann showed in 1859 that those zeros control the error term in how the primes are distributed. So the hypothesis is equivalent to saying the primes are as evenly spread as they could possibly be. It's one of the 7 Clay Millennium problems, with a 1-million-dollar prize, and an enormous body of mathematics is written in the form: assuming the Riemann hypothesis, then this.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: And the verification?

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: That's what makes this different from the usual crank claim. On Saturday, the Lean Focused Research Organization and the Mathlib Initiative put out a joint statement saying the files compile, the theorem stated matches the real Riemann hypothesis, and no extra unproven assumptions are smuggled in. They said they have full confidence the proof is correct. An independent end-to-end rebuild was still running as of Sunday. The Clay Institute still lists the problem as open.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: What are the mathematicians saying?

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Terence Tao called it an enormous Lean-only proof and said the strategy appears to use the full power of the Langlands program and arithmetic geometry. Brian Conrey, who has spent his career on the zeta function, told AFP it's really the biggest thing that's ever happened in mathematics. And Kevin Buzzard, who has done more than anyone to push Lean, made the sharp point: a correct Lean proof doesn't make any accompanying human paper correct. He also noted that others with similar access to frontier AI didn't find it.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: There's a second claim floating around, too.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: There is, and it's almost poignant. The same day, Ravi Vakil, president of the American Mathematical Society, posted a roughly 940-page manuscript on the generalised hypothesis by Alessandro Masullo, a young mathematician at Stanford, the product of about 12 years of work. Vakil released it early because of the AI news, and has since said readers using AI tools have found problems, and he makes no claim it's correct. So you have a decade of human labour overtaken in a day, and then checked by machines within the weekend.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Here's my question as the generalist. If nobody understands the proof, do we know anything?

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: We know that the statement is true, if the verification holds. We don't know why. Tao's worry is exactly that: a proof that settles whether, not why. Reportedly the idea Claude proposed is a chain of what are called theta lifts, transformations from the Langlands toolkit that move information between different kinds of symmetric functions, chained roughly square-root-of-X times for a sum of length X. A human now has to compress 17 million lines into an argument another human can hold in their head. That's the new job description: mathematicians go from finding proofs to understanding and explaining them, and to choosing which questions are worth asking.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: And the obvious worry: does this break encryption?

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: No. RSA rests on how hard it is to factor large numbers, and the Riemann hypothesis says nothing about factoring. What changes is that a pile of results that were conditional become unconditional. Miller's primality test, for instance, runs deterministically in polynomial time if the generalised hypothesis holds. That's a theory gain, not a security hole.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: What about the prize?

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Clay's rules want publication in a qualifying journal, 2 years of waiting, and general acceptance by the community. A Lean-only proof with an AI collaborator is a case the rules never imagined. Does formal verification count as acceptance? Can a model be a co-author? Those questions will run for years.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: And for the people on Friday selling every AI stock they own?

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: That's the irony I'd leave you with. The market just spent a week asking whether AI can earn a return, and on the same Friday, the strongest piece of evidence yet that frontier models can do genuinely new science arrived. Those aren't contradictions. Proving the Riemann hypothesis doesn't pay for a gigawatt data centre. But it does mean the bear case can't be that the technology is a parlour trick. The argument is about price and timing, not capability.

segments.raw: SEGMENT FOUR — ENERGY / DATA CENTERS / UTILITIES
segments.label: Energy / Data Centers / Utilities

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: To energy and data centres, and the biggest market for them just hit pause. On November 17, Loudoun County's supervisors voted 7 to 1, with 1 abstention, to pause final decisions on legislative data-centre and substation applications for up to 12 months, which the county says is the maximum Virginia law allows.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The word that matters is substation. About 33 active applications are caught. The 15 to 17 projects that are by-right or grandfathered keep moving, and staff review and Planning Commission hearings continue, so the county expects a 4 to 6 month backlog when the pause lifts. But including substations means the wires buildout in Data Center Alley slows too, and that hits projects already entitled, because they still need the transmission and distribution capacity to energise. Land in Northern Virginia that's already powered just became scarcer for at least a year. And the clock runs per application from its Planning Commission date, which land-use lawyers at Potomac Law already flag as open to challenge.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: And it isn't just Virginia.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: San Jose approved a pause the same day on data-centre and large-energy-use approvals until its standards vote on December 8, covering about a dozen projects, including Google's 250-megawatt site in Alviso. Two of the deepest data-centre markets in America moving to pause in the same week is a political signal, not a zoning quirk.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Then PJM. Consumer advocates from 7 states, Ohio, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Maryland, Delaware, West Virginia and Illinois, with the market monitor's backing, asked PJM's board on November 18 to seek FERC approval to postpone the 2029 to 2030 capacity auction, scheduled for December 9 to 15.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Their argument is that the load forecast is inflated by data-centre requests that won't materialise. The planning parameters forecast a 171,916-megawatt peak, up 5,963 megawatts or 3.6% on the year before, with a reliability requirement of 158,712 megawatts. The market monitor estimates that keeping the speculative data-centre load in the forecast adds 5 to 10 billion dollars in customer costs. The July auction cleared right at the cap, and the FERC-approved collar is a cap of 337.83 dollars per megawatt-day and a floor of 181.91. PJM's spokesman says a delay could destabilise the market.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Who wins if it's delayed?

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Ratepayers in the short run, merchant generators lose. A cleaner forecast means a lower clearing price and less capacity revenue for Constellation, Vistra, Talen. And it would set a precedent that the auction waits for a verified load book, which pushes the cost of speculative large-load requests back onto the requesters, through collateral and take-or-pay tariffs. Watch for a board decision this week, because a FERC filing has to move fast to beat December 9.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: And the read-through from Friday's sell-off?

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The market is splitting the sector. Regulated utilities with contracted load held up as a hiding place. Constellation was reportedly down around 15% on the week, Nebius fell 16% on Friday, and Caterpillar dropped on fears that data-centre construction is slowing. On Nvidia, look at the guide: 130 billion dollars for the fourth quarter, but it's a 14-week quarter, so the weekly run rate is only about 4% above the third quarter. That deceleration is what the market heard. On the credit side, PIMCO says investment-grade bonds backed by data centres leased to hyperscalers trade about 146 basis points wide of the tenant's own debt, down from about 180 in late September, and it expects that gap to tighten, because slower building means less new supply of that paper.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: So lenders don't walk away, they reprice.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Exactly. Expect tighter termination and take-or-pay terms in leases, and expect 2027 hyperscaler capex guides at fourth-quarter earnings to be judged on growth rate, not absolute dollars. And one date for Texas: the Abbott directive from August still freezes pending ERCOT data-centre interconnections until each one passes an audit, in a large-load queue of more than 474 gigawatts, about 90% of it data centres. The audit filing is reportedly due around December 10, with the PUC meeting around December 19. Until then, in Texas, behind-the-meter gas, fuel cells and on-site storage are the only way to hold a schedule.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Oras na para sa ating bokabularyo sa Tagalog. Dalawang salita ngayong umaga, parehong galing sa mga balita sa Maynila.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Ang una ay saksi. Ito ang taong nakakita o nakakaalam ng isang pangyayari at nagpapatotoo tungkol dito. Sa korte, ang saksi ang tinatawag para magsalita sa ilalim ng panunumpa. Puwede ring pandiwa: sumaksi, o naging saksi.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: May kapatid itong salita, ang testigo, galing sa Espanyol. Mas pormal at mas makaluma ang testigo, madalas sa mga lumang dokumento at sa usapang abogado. Ang saksi naman ay katutubo at pang-araw-araw. Sinasabi natin, saksi ako sa kasal nila, o saksi ang buong barangay sa nangyari.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: At pansinin ang malalim na gamit: ang saksi ng estado, o state witness, ay ang akusadong pinalaya mula sa kaso kapalit ng kanyang patotoo. Mabigat iyon, dahil ang dating kasabwat ay nagiging susi ng tagausig.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Ang ikalawa ay gugulin. Ito ang perang gagastusin o ilalaan para sa isang layunin. Mula ito sa ugat na gugol, na ang ibig sabihin ay gastos o paggastos.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Ihambing natin sa gastos. Ang gastos ay pang-araw-araw: malaki ang gastos ko sa pamasahe. Ang gugulin ay mas pormal at pang-badyet, kaya madalas marinig sa Kongreso at sa mga ulat ng pamahalaan: ang mga gugulin ng pamahalaan, o ang taunang gugulin para sa edukasyon.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: At may kaugnay na pandiwa: gumugol. Gumugol siya ng sampung taon sa pananaliksik. Kaya ang gugulin ay hindi lang pera; puwede ring panahon at lakas na inilaan. Pakinggan ninyo ang dalawang salitang ito sa susunod na bahagi.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Sumuko sa NBI noong Huwebes si Felicito Guevarra, presidente ng Samchan Foreign Exchange at isa sa mga kapwa akusado sa 7.4 bilyong pisong kasong plunder laban kay dating Speaker Martin Romualdez. Binigyan siya ng Ombudsman ng kondisyonal na imyunidad para maging saksi ng estado, kapalit ng mga rekord at gadget ng kanyang kumpanya.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Ngayong hapon naman, sisimulan ng Senado ang pagtalakay sa plenaryo ng mga gugulin ng pamahalaan para sa 2027, habang nagwewelga ang Manibela sa Kalakhang Maynila.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: On the Guevarra detail: he surrendered at the Santuario de San Antonio parish in Forbes Park, after prosecutors moved to cancel his passport. The conditions of his immunity are that he hands over Samchan's records and devices, stays in the country and stays under Justice Department protection. The Office of the Special Prosecutor has asked the Sandiganbayan's Third Division to drop him from the case and keep him in NBI custody for his own safety.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: That's the inflection point in the flood-control scandal. A money changer turned state witness means prosecutors can try to trace the cash, not just the contracts. Romualdez's lawyers say the transactions only show he sold dollars to a licensed money changer, which is exactly the argument a records-based witness is meant to test. And Zaldy Co is still a fugitive.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: On the budget, the Senate opens plenary debate on the 2027 spending bill at 1 this afternoon, on a budget of roughly 7.2 trillion pesos. Senate President Win Gatchalian says Congress can ratify before December 17, with second reading around December 3 and third reading December 10 to 12, then the bicameral conference. Finance chair JV Ejercito rejected the Makabayan bloc's demand that the House recall its version over provisions the Supreme Court has ruled unconstitutional.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: And the commute today: Manibela starts a 2-day transport strike, possibly 3, with more than 6,000 police deployed in Metro Manila. It's not about fuel prices. Manibela is backing LTO chief Markus Lacanilao against his reported removal, which Transport Secretary Vince Dizon won't confirm.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: And the pressure on the peso shows in the balance of payments.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The Bangko Sentral reported an October deficit of 1.5 billion dollars, against a surplus of 706 million a year ago. That takes January to October to a 10.6-billion-dollar deficit, already past the central bank's own full-year forecast of 9.2 billion with 2 months to go. Gross reserves slipped to about 98 billion dollars, which the BSP put down to its foreign-exchange operations, lower gold valuations and debt payments. Read that with Friday's peso at 63.81: the BSP is spending reserves to slow the slide, and with gold down another 4.6% on Friday, the reserve number has a second leak. It strengthens the case for a hike at the December 17 meeting.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Now Mandarin, with 2 items for this morning's China story on interest rates.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The first is a connective pair: 要么…要么, yàome… yàome, meaning either… or. It frames a forced choice between 2 options, and it leans spoken, the register of a trader or an editorial, not a statute. Example: 央行要么降息，要么继续等待，没有第三条路。(The central bank either cuts rates or keeps waiting; there is no third way.)

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Contrast it with 或者 and 还是. 或者 just offers alternatives in a statement, you can come Monday or Tuesday, with no pressure. 还是 asks the question: 你喝茶还是咖啡？(Tea or coffee?) 要么…要么 is the one with an edge: these are the only 2 options, pick one. The formal written cousin is 或者…或者, which loses that sense of ultimatum.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The second is 维持, wéichí, to maintain, to keep something at its current level. It's formal, written register, and it's the verb financial news uses for a central bank holding rates. It collocates with 不变, unchanged, as in 维持不变, and with 现状, the status quo, 稳定, stability, and 生活, a livelihood. Example: 央行连续第18个月维持贷款市场报价利率不变。(The central bank kept the loan prime rate unchanged for an 18th straight month.)

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: And against 保持: 保持 is broader and more neutral, to keep, as in 保持联系, keep in touch, or 保持冷静, stay calm. 维持 has a sense of effort against pressure, holding something up that might otherwise slip. You 维持 order, a ceasefire, a peg. Listen for both in the China story next.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: 物价还在下跌，央行要么降息，要么继续维持利率不变，这次它又选择了等待。(Prices are still falling, and the central bank either cuts rates or keeps holding them unchanged; this time it chose to wait again.)

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: On Friday, the 1-year loan prime rate held at 3% and the 5-year at 3.5%, the 18th straight month at record lows, as 23 of 28 economists in a Reuters poll expected. The bigger news is plumbing: earlier this month the People's Bank made the overnight reverse repo its main policy rate and said loan pricing will rely less on the loan prime rate.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: And through the two-speed lens?

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Nominal rates frozen while prices fall means real borrowing costs stay high for exactly the part of the economy that's weakest: households in lower-tier cities, private developers, local-government financing vehicles. In October, new-home prices in third- and fourth-tier cities were down 2% from a year earlier and resale prices 6.5%, even after the September mortgage subsidy of 1 point a year for first homes. Meanwhile, the IMF puts LGFV debt at around 64 trillion yuan, roughly 4 and a half times Beijing's official hidden-debt figure. Citi doesn't expect cuts until 2027, and then only 2 of 10 basis points. The fast half of the economy, exporters and the AI-chip push, doesn't need cheaper money. The slow half needs it and isn't getting it. And this weekend Beijing chose to ease margin-financing rules for the stock market instead. That's a choice to support asset prices before it supports borrowers.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Arts and culture, and the week's most revealing auction lot is one that never sold. Hours before Christie's New York evening sale on November 17, the house withdrew Frida Kahlo's Congreso de los pueblos por la paz, from 1952, lot 72A, estimated at 2.5 to 3.5 million dollars. Mexico's national institute of fine arts, INBAL, had asked Christie's to postpone and to produce full provenance, and an activist group, Defendamos la Colección Gelman, says the painting appears in Diego Rivera's 1957 inventory for the Casa Azul trust.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: And the legal knot is genuinely tangled. Mexico's 1984 decree bars the permanent export of Kahlo works that were in the country at the time, and this painting reportedly left decades before that. INBAL itself has previously argued that a sale abroad would be legal,. Christie's said it withdrew the lot for further research and looks forward to selling it later. The critic's point is about where value comes from now. Kahlo is the clearest case of an artist whose market is set as much by heritage law and national sentiment as by bidders. A 3-million-dollar estimate is modest for her; the real price is the risk that a buyer owns something they can never lend to a Mexican museum.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: And in Venice, the Biennale closed on Sunday.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Koyo Kouoh's exhibition, In Minor Keys, drew 714,015 visitors, with a record 100 national participations and under-26s about a quarter of the audience, even though the run was about 3 weeks shorter than usual. It was a show completed after Kouoh's death in 2025, and it will be remembered for its awards fight. The international jury resigned en masse on April 30 after saying it would not consider countries whose leaders face International Criminal Court charges, which was read as Russia and Israel. The Biennale replaced the Golden and Silver Lions with 2 Visitors' Lions voted by ticket holders, and more than 50 artists withdrew from consideration. The winners are expected this week. Whatever wins, a public vote that many of the artists refused to enter is a strange way for the world's oldest biennale to crown anyone, and the Russian pavilion stayed shut all year.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Next stop for the market is Art Basel Miami Beach, December 4 to 6, with 272 exhibitors, including El Apartamento, the first Cuba-based gallery at the Miami fair, and Rosana Paulino's first bronze at Mendes Wood. It lands after a November sales week that came in about 3% below combined low estimates.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Op-eds. First, James Mackintosh in his Streetwise column for The Wall Street Journal on Sunday, under the headline: Has the AI Bubble Already Burst? His argument is that the mini-bubble in data-centre and chip stocks has already deflated, and that whether the larger AI bubble is going too is unknowable but, in his words, frighteningly plausible. He walks through the dot-com parallels, some remarkably similar, some worse, some better, and he points to Korea as the warning, where retail investors piled into memory-chip stocks with borrowed money. His chain is: tighter funding, then data-centre capex cuts, then supplier revenue falling, then lenders pulling back.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The steelman is strong, because that chain is mechanically correct, and Friday showed the first link. But the counter is that this doesn't look like 2000 on the numbers. Nvidia at around 13 and a half times forward earnings is priced like a cyclical, not a bubble stock. Hyperscaler earnings are still growing and their capex is funded mostly from cash flow, not from junk bonds sold to retail. Korea's crash says more about retail margin debt than about AI demand. What we're living through looks like a valuation reset in the middle of a real buildout. The difference matters: a burst bubble means the capex stops; a reset means it continues at a lower multiple and a slower growth rate.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Second, Richard Haass at Project Syndicate, written before the Shenzhen summit, under the headline Yalta in Shenzhen? His line: The best to be hoped for from the summit of Trump, Xi, and Putin is nothing. The argument is that any grand bargain would have meant a Yalta-style carve-up into spheres of influence over Ukraine or Taiwan, so a summit that produces nothing is a summit that gave nothing away. And the thin communiqué that came out of it seems to bear him out.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: The counter-take, from Michael McFaul among others, is that nothing wasn't free. The photograph alone was a gift to Putin: a leader under an International Criminal Court warrant standing as an equal beside the presidents of America and China, in a format that excluded Europe and Ukraine. My view is that both are right on different timescales. Haass is right that no deal was signed. McFaul is right that the trilateral format itself is the concession, and Berlin's Coalition of the Willing meeting that same week was Europe's answer to it.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: And our one good thing. In 1967, Russell Jacobson, a Navy corpsman in Vietnam, was shot several times and wounded by a grenade. While he was recovering in hospital, students at St. Ann School in Gloucester, Massachusetts, wrote him 33 letters. His family says reading them is what got him back onto his feet. His wife, Peggy, kept every one of them for nearly 60 years.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Now his son, Dave Jacobson, is tracking down each of those letter-writers, children then, grandparents now, to thank them in person for what they did for his father. So far he has found 18 of the 33. That's 18 people who wrote a note to a stranger in the 1960s, and are only now learning it mattered.

turns.speaker: SAM
turns.text: Here's to the other 15. Write the note. That's The Morning Commute for Monday, November 23. I'm Sam.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: And I'm Alex. Have a good week.
